synthesis:draft.headline: SA1 five‑minute peak RRP 4981.0 $/MWh at 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z (2026-07-31 02:05 ACST)
summary: Peak dispatch RRP 4981.0 $/MWh at interval-ending 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z (2026-07-31 02:05 ACST).
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at that interval was 1472.82 MW and NETINTERCHANGE was −82.59 MW (net flow into SA1).

The analysis window (2026-07-30T04:30:00Z–2026-07-31T05:00:00Z) included 214 five‑minute intervals at-or-above the analysis threshold; the unweighted mean five‑minute RRP in the window was 416.71 $/MWh.
AEMO market notice reports a City West transformer trip (City West 275/66 kV transformer T_1 and circuit breaker 6675) described as a 'Non-credible contingency event' [c1].
AEMO market notice reports a short‑notice outage of the Belalie‑Davenport 275kV line at 1630 hrs and the invocation of constraint set(s) including S-DVBL_BC-2CP [c2].
Unit-level SCADA observations show sizable output changes during the window, for example BARKIPS rose by 192.45 MW and CGBESS changed by −47.91 MW (bidirectional battery observation).

possible_explanations.statement: The short‑notice outage of the Belalie‑Davenport 275kV line reported by AEMO (market notice [c2]) might have reduced interconnector transfer capability or invoked constraint(s) that affected dispatch conditions and price outcomes.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare five‑minute NETINTERCHANGE values and constraint binding flags before and after the notice time (see ev0438 for NETINTERCHANGE at the peak) and retrieve the Network Outage Scheduler entry and the invoked constraint set S-DVBL_BC-2CP equations referenced in market notice [c2].

possible_explanations.statement: The 'Non-credible contingency event' reporting the City West transformer trip (market notice [c1]) might have influenced later dispatch patterns or reserve availability during the day and so might be related to altered dispatch outcomes.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Examine the sequence of constraint activations and dispatch instruction logs after the transformer event, and align those with unit dispatch and price movements; retrieve constraint history and dispatch logs for the period referenced in market notice [c1].

possible_explanations.statement: Large observed unit output changes (example: BARKIPS +192.45 MW ev0940; CGBESS −47.91 MW ev0955) might have changed local supply availability or operational responses in the five‑minute dispatch intervals around the peak.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Align unit-level SCADA traces (ev0940, ev0955, ev0939) to the five‑minute price timeline and inspect corresponding bids/offers and any binding constraint equations to see whether these units were flagged or constrained during the high‑price intervals.

The SCADA unit changes are descriptive snapshots and do not by themselves indicate outages, bid changes or instructions; confirming operational status changes requires dispatch/market offer records.
